meaning: money is hard to get, so you should spend it carefully
example: I wanted a new bike, but money doesn't grow on trees, so I waited until my birthday.
origin: A common English saying that reminds people money must be earned through work; its exact origin is unclear.

wrong_meanings.meaning: money can be found easily in nature
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This is the literal reading of the words, but the idiom is about how hard money is to earn.

wrong_meanings.meaning: to become very rich very quickly
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This describes the opposite idea; the idiom warns against spending too freely, not about getting rich fast.

wrong_meanings.meaning: to plant money in the garden to make it grow
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This is a silly literal image that has no connection to the idiomatic meaning.

explanation: 'Money doesn't grow on trees' means money must be earned, so it should be spent carefully. It is often used when someone wants to remind others to avoid wasting money.
